articleTitle: Trends of digital society development towards 5G technology
abstract: The development of every new generation of wireless communications begins with increased requirements for speed and capacity. In addition to the above, the 5G (5th generation) systems must also satisfy new scenarios of using very different requirements, including various ways of communicating the devices. Several research initiatives address the issues of regulation and standardization in this area. In this paper, we gave a brief overview of research on future 5G systems, the requirements they are facing, user scenarios, functionalities, and KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) as a measure of assessing the performances of these systems.

articleTitle: Short-term wind forecasting based on time series data for dynamic line rating
abstract: This paper presents a short description of the dynamic line rating (DLR) technology, and realized pilot project for increasing transmission capacity of overhead power lines. The method based on time series for short-term wind speed/direction forecasting was presented together with the test results obtained with several models. Analyzing the results it is concluded that some of the models could be used for wind speed forecasting.

articleTitle: A new algorithm for energy-efficient IEEE 802.11 access points
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm for increasing energy efficiency of individual IEEE 802.11 WAPs (Wi-Fi Access Points). The algorithm is trained based on monitoring Traffic Flow, Clients/Subscribers Flow and RF coverage map Flow, using cross-correlation to determine the optimal Traffic Level Filling by WAPs during the observed time period. WAPs are managed by central monitoring system to increase the energy efficiency. The proposed algorithm enables a significant percentage increase in energy efficiency for IEEE 802.11 WAPs systems.

articleTitle: Two-way space shift keying with relay selection
abstract: In this paper, a two-way multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) space shift keying (SSK) scheme with relay selection is proposed for amplify-and-forward relaying. In this scheme, the sources exchange their SSK symbols via a selected relay node. We derive a theoretical upper-bound expression and we also perform an asymptotic performance analysis for the average error probability of the proposed system. It is shown that the proposed system outperforms conventional two-way SSK scheme without relay selection.

articleTitle: On luminance reduction in high dynamic range synthetic aperture radar images
abstract: High dynamic range images enable more detailed information regarding the content. By performing luminance compression, images can be prepared for the traditional low dynamic range reproduction. There are numerous ways to perform the compression (tone-mapping), but the content may affect the image quality. The reduction of dynamic range may produce unwanted effects (e.g. due to noise) and can be tailored for specific image content. In this paper we analyze several examples related to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) as images with high dynamic range.

articleTitle: Simple efficient digital filters for specific applications: DC blockers
abstract: In numerous digital signal processing applications, the data are collected by using low cost, imperfect, digital sensors. This is the case in low cost sensor networks and simple devices which are used in the Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The most common artifacts are DC bias and high frequency noise. Therefore, there is a need for simple efficient digital filters for such applications. In this paper, we analyze the usability of DC blocker, its fixed point implementation, general linear-phase DC blocker, and simple lowpass digital filter. We test performance of these filters in processing real world ECG data.

articleTitle: Recommender systems in the big data environment using Mahout framework
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to demonstrate the application possibilities of the Mahout framework in the Big Data environment with the goal to improve customer service through a recommender system. The paper describes the method of applying machine learning for analysis, processing, and visualization of data collected from an e-commerce store server. The practical application of this system can meet the users' needs and assist in finding personalized content.

articleTitle: Improving the azimuth resolution of stripmap SAR image using Adaptive Weighted Norm Extrapolation
abstract: The content - This paper describes the procedure of application Adaptive Weighted Norm Extrapolation (AWNE) method on stripmap SAR image which was formed using Doppler Beam Sharpening (DBS) algorithm, in order to improve resolution in the azimuth axis. The characteristics of stripmap SAR recording are listed, as well as the causes of poor resolution in the azimuth axis of the DBS algorithm. Before using the AWNE method, the SAR data were modified in the azimuth axis. The result is that the resolution of the signal in the frequency domain is improved, which represents resolution improvement in the azimuth axis of stripmap SAR image.

articleTitle: A novel solution for an ECU simulator as a key component for automated testing and verification of a vehicle diagnostic device
abstract: In this paper a generic, configurable solution for an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) simulator is described. The ECU simulator is a component of an Automated Testing System that aims at testing and verifying new devices for vehicle diagnostics. A vehicle has many electronic control units that are communicating over various automotive protocols. The vehicle diagnostic device must be able to communicate with all the ECUs. One of the key components in the automated test system is the ECU simulator that is able to simulate any of the ECUs, communicating with various automotive protocols, simulating any possible state. In this paper, the solution for the challenging task of designing and implementing the ECU simulator is presented.

articleTitle: Applicability of the ECGalert solution
abstract: Wireless ECG patches have been extensively used for long-term monitoring of the patient and to help detect heart problems that cannot be captured within 24h monitoring. In this paper, we present how the ECGalert technology has successfully been used to detect serious heart problems as a long-term monitoring device. We present the features of the solution and a use case of applicability.

articleTitle: PHY based Jamming attacks against OFDM systems: A measurement study
abstract: We consider a novel jamming attack that jointly targets the cyclic prefix (CP) and pilot symbols. The deteriorating performance of this attack is compared with the known techniques, including barrage jamming, CP based jamming, pilot jamming and pilot nulling attacks through a software define radio (SDR) based implementation. The communication performance between transmitter and receiver under distinct attacks is monitored through error vector magnitude (EVM), bit error rate (BER) and modulation error ratio (MER) measurements.

articleTitle: Application of huge pages to the netmap platform
abstract: The netmap platform has been designed to support fast exchange of packets between user applications and the external world. Hardware of powerful servers can support multiple 10 Gb/s ports, but, the software cannot process shortest packets at such high throughputs even when it utilized the netmap platform. Such performance indicates that there is a room for improvements of the netmap platform. Translation of virtual memory addresses to physical memory addresses might be one of bottlenecks that slow down packet processing. This translation can be simplified and sped up by utilization of huge pages, as their number is smaller. In this paper, we will explore improvements that can be achieved by utilization of huge pages within the netmap based applications. We will demonstrate that the significant packet rate increase can be achieved by utilization of huge pages.

articleTitle: Evaluating application-layer traffic optimization cost metrics for P2P multimedia streaming
abstract: To help users of P2P communication systems perform better-than-random selection of communication peers, Internet Engineering Task Force standardized the Application Layer Traffic Optimization (ALTO) protocol. The ALTO provided data-routing cost metric, can be used to rank peers in P2P communication systems. However, the method to derive the data-routing cost metric is undefined by the standard. This paper proposes and evaluates three methods to derive the data-routing cost metric for use in ALTO servers.

articleTitle: Advanced algorithm for scheduling TM transactions with conflict avoidance
abstract: In this paper we developed the AAC algorithm, which surpasses the limitations of the previouslu developed AC algorithm, and which always finds the transaction schedule without conflicts and with minimal span. Additionally, new AAC algorithm was validated, and its performance was compared with the performance of RR, ETLB, and AC algorithms on a processor with four cores, and on the test loads of various levels of concurrency.

articleTitle: Experiences in the teaching of a new computing paradigm: DataFlow supercomputing
abstract: If a new paradigm is presented before experienced professionals, even if it already demonstrates superiority, the presentation is typically received with resistance. If a new paradigm already demonstrates superiority, and it is presented before students, it is typically received with enthusiasm, especially if tools are available that enable the paradigm to be utilized with a relative ease, and even more if a library of useful examples is at the disposal of new users. Over a period of time, these students grow into experienced professionals who accept the new paradigm, at their new industrial posts, without any resistance. With the above in mind, a series of courses was organized for universities in the USA and Europe, to teach the data flow computing paradigm, using the Maxeler approach as the baseline for practical work. The courses were organized on three different levels: (A) One-hour presentations, followed by another hour about the programming model, and a hands-on hour with tools, (B) A certified full-day short-course that students could use in their transcripts as a diploma supplement, and (C) A one-semester course for 1, 2, or 3 credits that students could use as a graduation requirement. Different presentation levels require different methods of presentation and produce different results in the dissemination domain. These results are here presented for 10 universities in the group A, 10 in the group B, and 10 in the group C. Where appropriate, the findings are backed with statistics data.

articleTitle: Enhanced bandwidth PIFA antennas for 900/1800 MHz and WiFi 2400 MHz band with a dielectric cover
abstract: This paper is dedicated to the development of PIFA antennas with a dielectric cover for different frequency bands. A PIFA antenna on FR-4 with ε = 4.4 and thickness h = 2 mm was simulated, manufactured and tested for use with the GSM 900/1800 MHz transceiver. On the same substrate, an antenna for Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) was designed. For antennas, regions of 65 by 10 and 45 by 10 millimeters respectively were allocated. The antennas have a double-layered cover made of polyethylene and polyurethane with dielectric constants of 1.2 to 1.5 and 6 to 8 respectively.

articleTitle: Cooperative architecture of data acquisition for emission reduction in traffic
abstract: Increasing fuel prices, short-term inventories with CO2 emission growth worldwide have contributed to the development of technology in auto industry. Many advanced technologies in the auto industry have emerged in the last decade, but with little focus on driver behavior to reduce fuel consumption. With the implementation of cooperative intelligent transport system (C-ITS) architecture for data acquisition from the vehicles it is possible to achieve defined energy and environmental requirements in traffic. In this paper the areas of application of C-ITS in terms of support for eco-driving will be defined and presented. Also, the implementation of presented system can have the influence on traffic flow and other traffic parameters, but defines new requirements for other involved subsystems (driver-vehicle-infrastructure).

articleTitle: Architecture of a system for stimulating intellectual activity with adaptive environment SMILE
abstract: We present an architecture of a system for stimulating intellectual activities of elderly. The system adapts to the user and is specially designed for older people using simple interface avoiding complex graphical solutions. Our goal is to use an IPTV as a device that is mostly used by elderly and integrate voice assistants, social networks, reminders and self-care system into a service offered to elderly. This will improve their quality of life by keeping intellectual activity on a high level with stimulation environment.

articleTitle: A novel MIMO antenna design with AMC reflector
abstract: We propose a low-cost, dual band (2.4-5.2 GHz) and dual band (2.4-5.8 GHz) MIMO antennas by using two identical T shaped antenna with high isolation. MIMO is a technique that is used a multiple number of antennas as a transmitter and a receiver. Using artificial magnetic conductor as a reflector made our antenna low profile and high isolated. A dual-band MIMO antenna with high isolation by using artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is proposed.

articleTitle: Channel impulse response estimation using vector network analyzer
abstract: This paper describes the results of frequency-domain indoor radio channel characterization using vector network analyzer in the 1.7–1.9 GHz frequency band. Channel impulse response estimate was obtained via inverse Fourier transform through repeated measurements of its transfer function. Statistical parameters of radio propagation, namely the channel's power delay profile and cumulative distributions of root mean square delay spread, mean excess delay and coherence bandwidth were evaluated and comparisons with results in literature were drawn.

articleTitle: Understanding customers' behaviour of telecommunication companies increasing the efficiency of clustering techniques
abstract: The customers' data of Telecommunication Companies represent a powerful tool to explore their behaviour and then to increase their satisfaction. The data produced is too large to extract on time useful information, which could be beneficial for both sides, companies and customers. One of the solutions to explore this data is representing it by the adoption of clustering techniques. In this work, two distributed / multi-core versions of clustering algorithms were used, namely DBSCAN and k-means, which both of them cluster data according to its characteristics. While DBSCAN is a density-based spatial clustering algorithm and groups data based on the minimum size of participating objects per cluster and the minimum required distance between them, k-means clusters the data objects according the pre-desired number of groups. Thus, since the two methods use different roads to group the data objects, they form different clusters but each one has its importance depending on the characteristics of the applied method. The experiment results of both proposed distributed / multi-core techniques proved their efficiency.

articleTitle: Miniaturized microstrip bandpass filters with resonators
abstract: A novel microstrip bandpass filter design with two spiral resonators is presented in this paper. The proposed filter has good frequency selectivity and its dimensions are smaller in comparison with conventional ones. A numerical simulation of the filter with the central frequency of 2000 MHz was made to receive the S-parameters. A prototype with dimensions of 18.9 × 5 = 94.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was implemented on a substrate with a dielectric constant ϵ = 4.4, dielectric loss tangent tgδ = 0.02 and thickness h = 1.5 mm. The measured characteristics are in good agreement with the results of the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: GPS jamming mitigation through Taguchi's optimization method
abstract: This paper describes an adaptive antenna array that is able to spatially filter out multiple jamming signals from different directions using Taguchi's Optimization Method. A GPS antenna should cover a wide spatial angle to receive the maximum number of GPS signals but not too wide because jamming signals usually comes from a low elevation angle. Proposed system uses MUSIC algorithm to estimate DOA of jammers and Taguchi's Optimization Method to find optimum amplitude weight values in order to steer radiation nulls toward the jammer's directions while maintain the main beam constant. Proposed system can easily be replaced with conventional GPS antenna to improve GPS receiver jamming mitigation capabilities.

articleTitle: Identification of factors relevant for the estimation of smartphone life cycle
abstract: The smartphone industry is a fast-evolving industry with a bright future as smartphones became everyone's daily habit. This paper gathers existing research knowledge and provides the identification of factors that affect the stakeholders and the length of smartphone life cycle. Socio-demographic, economic, technological and psychological factors are found relevant by using comparative and compilation methods. Further aim of this research is to use the identified factors in a following research on life cycle estimation.

articleTitle: Simulation of operation and analysis of filters for stabilizing output voltages of the inverters
abstract: Application of Pulse Width Modulation, PWM, for stabilization of output voltage of transistor IGBT inverter upgrades its performances, but step-shaped voltage occurred due to operating regime of the transistor reduces its application as the universal voltage source. At the stabilization of the voltage mean value at the output of the inverter and due to the change of coefficients of non-linear distortions, the amplitude value of voltage changes over wide limits. In addition, the transmission of step-shaped voltages with large slopes (rectangular) using cables creates high level of interferences that can impair the operation of electric equipment. Sinusoidal shape of the voltage, which has great advantages over the rectangular and is the most difficult to obtain even in the case of IGBT inverters, is obtained by using the conventional passive reactive filters because they are cheaper comparing to other devices for reducing the effects of harmonics. These filters contain passive elements (inductance, capacitance, resistance) and are set to frequencies of currents or voltages they have to cancel.

articleTitle: Comparison metrics for the output of a mixed fixed point and floating point graphics pipeline
abstract: We propose to provide an analysis of some already existing and newly proposed metrics used for comparing altered images. The goal is to be able to accurately and objectively evaluate the alteration produced by an inaccurate, hybrid graphics pipeline that uses multiple real number formats relative to a fully accurate one. In order to obtain this, we have modified our own OpenGL ES 1.1 software implementation so that it could operate with different representations of real numbers. We fed this hybrid pipeline with about 2500 3D objects and rendered them in 180 frames for each object, in different positions, using a combination of real number formats across the pipeline. By using this setup we have obtained about 450000 reference images and about 2700000 altered ones. Finally, we obtained the differences between the two sets of images and tried to analyze them by using different metrics so that we could distinguish between acceptable altered images and non acceptable ones.

articleTitle: Path quality estimator for wireless sensor networks fast deployment tool
abstract: This paper introduces novel quality estimator that uses different metrics to decide the best paths towards the root in Wireless Sensor Networks. This quality function is used during deployment stage, ensuring nodes are located optimally and nimbly. This mechanism will help WSNs' adoption in Industrial Internet of Things applications.

articleTitle: Universal multimedia access and network coding — Working together for best user multimedia experience
abstract: In this paper are presented the main idea and architecture of Universal Multimedia Access (UMA) and the fundamentals of network coding. A simulation study was conducted for advantages of network coding, compared to conventional transmission.

articleTitle: A new channel-aware LTE-A uplink resource allocation scheduling algorithm
abstract: New cellular networks standardized by 3GPP as LTE and LTE-A aim to provide scalable resources optimizing both system performance and user satisfaction. In order to achieve this goal the scheduler algorithm becomes of upmost importance. Thus a number of different resource allocation algorithms have been suggested. However, the uplink has been little covered due to the fact it poses more specific constraints and it is quite complicated to balance the trade-off between channel state information, system throughput and user perceived throughput. In this paper we propose a new resource allocation algorithm that tries to balance the advantages of two previously suggested ones. We also introduce a new parameter, the user ratio, which allows us to explicitly quantify the trade-off between fairness, system throughput and user throughput for different channel conditions.

articleTitle: A concept of efficient parking in smart cities
abstract: With the development of information and telecommunication technologies, their application in everyday life is increasingly being emphasized in order to improve the quality of the same. The possibilities of collecting data from sensors, advanced techniques for their processing, then collective knowledge and intelligence are combined in order to create an efficient environment for users in terms of health, administration, learning, economic development, etc. Accordingly, this paper describes the concept of smart cities, as well as one solution for parking regulation in cities in Serbia using the mobile application „Find My Parking“.

articleTitle: UHI boot protocol implementation in Android emulator for MIPS architecture
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the UHI boot protocol support implemented for the MIPS Ranchu virtual board used by Android emulator. This protocol is not supported by all boards and kernel versions, but provision is made for supporting boards which use a legacy boot protocol. The paper describes the solution implemented on both emulator and kernel side.

articleTitle: Rapid programming of embedded autonomous robots
abstract: This paper presents a fast and accurate method for programming simple strategies for small autonomous robots based on embedded processing platforms. There are several approaches in programming of mobile and industrial robots, but the most common one is online programming. This method begins with so called teaching phase during which human operator guides the robot by issuing a set of simple commands. All that commands are automatically logged and saved into a command log, which in the operation phase eventually serves as final program. In case of industrial robots, the whole process including teaching and operation phase runs on the same platform, usually PC, which by the rule has convenient user interface. On the other side, small embedded robot platforms do not have appropriate user interfaces and their programs must be written in the form of hard-coded precompiled firmware. This paper describes the architecture of the robot and supporting system which are designed in the way that support convenient usage of PC based software during development phase, and a fast and accurate method for translation of tested command sequence into the embedded platform firmware running the robot during the deployment phase.

articleTitle: Efficient hardware realization of digital image decoder
abstract: In this paper, efficient hardware realization of digital image decoder, has been described. Each block, the proposed image decoder consists of (entropy decoder, decoder probability estimator, dequantizer and inverse subband transformer), has been developed with intention to optimize the hardware architecture and reduce the amount of used logic and memory resources in separate blocks themselves, as well as in the entire image decoder. The proposed realization has been verified by implementation within a low cost FPGA chip.

articleTitle: Kidney stone classification with electromagnetic properties: Preliminary results
abstract: This work focuses on classification of 3 types of kidney stones using their electrical properties. The electrical properties of kidney stones were determined by utilizing the open-ended coaxial probe method in the range of 500MHz-6GHz. The specified dielectric and conductivity properties are classified using the `k' nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm.

articleTitle: One solution of complex ADAS HW system testing
abstract: The trend of installing Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in vehicles is entering from the “desired” to “mandatory requirement” phase. In addition, the number of features supported multiplies with each new generation of ADAS. With increased production and growing number of ADAS features, increases the time to test the functionality. Thus, it is necessary to automate the process of testing hardware architecture of ADAS. This paper presents one such solution on ALPHA AMV platform. Paper also describes architecture of TDA2xx SoC of ALPHA development platform and methods of testing components of ALPHA platform.

articleTitle: Using digital and mobile technologies for increasing efficiency of financial institutions
abstract: Possibilities and methods for increasing efficiency of financial institutions operation using digital and mobile electronic technologies are considered, proposed and presented in the paper. Digital and mobile electronic technologies are used in many areas and many practical solutions and applications. One of very important areas is financial business in many financial institutions. Using computers, computer networks, Internet and smart mobile phones, with appropriate software applications, enable to increase speed and security of all financial transactions and increase financial institutions efficiency. Also, it gives many advantages to users of financial services and institutions. Way to increase efficiency of operation of financial institutions using digital and mobile technologies on the example of the typical commercial bank is proposed and described. As an example of using such technologies for increasing efficiency of the bank was designed, developed, implemented and described one system for facilitating and accelerating issuance of bank loans using smart mobile phones. Implementation, used technologies, possibilities, advantages for bank and user and way of using of the system are described.

articleTitle: 2 to 4 Decoder based on current logic
abstract: A new design concept of developing 2 to 4 decoders based on linear logic is considered. The circuit design and result of simulation on 0.25 um CMOS technology are presented. An advantages of the proposed approach such as low dependence from voltage supply, temperature and radiation are shown.

articleTitle: Serbian remote control of airport's weather stations SRCAWSII
abstract: In this paper we are presenting remote monitoring system for continuous supervision and automatic statistical reporting of meteorological sensors and automatic weather stations for Serbia and Montenegro Air Traffic Services SMATSA llc. Implemented solution enables monitoring and instant alarming of available meteorological equipment statuses in local airports technical service, and what is more important, real time centralized monitoring of all airports at the same time in headquarter office.

articleTitle: Improvement of GNU GDB for analyzing TLS variable from core file of target architecture
abstract: Usage of GNU GDB on the host machines during the analysis of core files that are created on embedded platforms with different architecture was denied for fetching value of TLS variable, but this document describes enhancement of the tool which implements that behavior and properly usage of the tool.

articleTitle: Carrier synchronization algorithm for software defined radio
abstract: Coherent receivers require carrier synchronization of a received signal, in order to achieve better demodulation characteristics then non-coherent receivers. Carrier synchronization of IEEE 802.15.4 signal is performed using preamble transmitted at beginning of packet. The traditional solution employs adjustment of passband frequency using Costas Loop circuitry. Software-defined radio requires carrier synchronization to be performed in baseband after demodulation. This paper represents the solution of phase synchronization for IEEE 802.15.4 coherent receiver on software defined radio.

articleTitle: Towards robust communication-based object monitoring under harsh propagation conditions
abstract: Battery-powered sensor nodes are available for various monitoring tasks. Among these, cargo trains pose some special challenges on both the nodes as well as the communication due to the harsh environmental conditions. In this paper, we present insight on propagation conditions in train scenarios based on theoretical simulations and real-world measurements and finally discuss options to achieve robust and reliable communication under the observed conditions. The discussion also includes requirements regarding quality of service and energy-efficiency.

articleTitle: Low-power wireless data acquisition system
abstract: State-of-the-art electronics being used by different consumers are increasingly requiring low power modes of operation and extended battery life. In this paper, the low-power component is integrated in a data acquisition system (DAQ), which can read important data about temperature, humidity and light intensity from the environment. The goal of the project is to design a DAQ that uses low-power and can be further integrated in other domain specific applications such as agriculture, sport and health. The obtained results demonstrate that the low-power desideratum can be attained by a specific set of actions.

articleTitle: Resonances of uniaxially anisotropic photonic nanoresonators
abstract: In this work we calculate the resonance frequencies of open spherical anisotropic nanoresonators. The theory used is based on the volume integral equation method which supports the anisotropic properties of modern nanomaterials used in photonic applications. The developed method is applied on the computation of the modes appearing in various photonic applications, like whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) lasing and interfacial refractive index sensing. The method proves accurate for the prediction of lower order as well as higher order modes. The theory is validated with comparisons to separation of variables method, and can be considered as a tool for the prediction and interpretation of experimental results.

articleTitle: Integracija digitalnog TV prijemnika na uređaje sa Android sistemom
abstract: Za prenos emitovanog digitalnog signala koristi se grupa standarda koje propisuje međunarodna organizacija Digital Video Broadcast. Digitalni televizijski prijemnik je uređaj koji za ulogu ima prijem digitalnog TV signala kao i njegovo obradu, prilagođavanje i reprodukciju na uređajima koji ovaj signal ne podržavaju. Android sistem ne poseduje predefinisanu programsku spregu za prijem i obradu digitalnog TV signala. Kako u okviru Linuks operativnog sistema postoji pomenuta podrška, a Android sistem je baziran na Linuks jezgru, javlja se ideja da se izvrši njena modifikacija i primeni na Android sistem.

articleTitle: Simultaneous characterization of bidirectional coupler and semiconductor photodetectors spectral properties
abstract: The method of simultaneous measurement of bidirectional coupler and semiconductor photodetectors spectral properties is presented. InGaAs and Ge photodiodes are used as photodetectors. The simulation of fiber-optic coupler spectral behavior, as well as the process of calculating fiber-optic coupler coupling ratio from data acquired by measurements is given. Furthermore, the responsivities of both photodetectors are calculated on the basis of the obtained coupling ratio.

articleTitle: Smart single-phase battery storage system
abstract: The continuous development of battery technologies (especially Li-Ion, LiFePO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) and photovoltaic systems allows the production of Battery Storage System (BSS) in the range of few kW up to the MW. BSS is primarily intended to the grid stabilization and peak-load coverage. However, BSS can be also used as an independent power source (with respect to macrogrid) and operate in the island mode. This paper describes the basic architecture and features of the single-phase BSS with smart control, monitoring and communication systems.

articleTitle: Study of substrate thickness influence on effectiveness of miniaturization, based on implementation of artificial transmission lines
abstract: In this paper we present an analysis of how the influence of the thickness of the material used on the efficiency of miniaturization of a branch-line coupler. The proposed method is based on replacing the traditional transmission line with an artificial transmission line. For the analysis was the application AWR Design Environment. Branch-line couplers with a substrate thickness of 1, 1.5 and 2 mm were designed and manufactured using standard methods for manufacturing printed circuit boards. According to the results obtained, it can be concluded that thickness affects the characteristics of the developed devices.

articleTitle: Efficient design of series-fed linear antenna arrays with ultralow sidelobes
abstract: Methods for solving some challenging tasks in the analysis of linear arrays with ultralow sidelobes are proposed. The design procedure based on them leads to a precise realization of the amplitude distribution while accounting for the mutual coupling at high antenna efficiency. Small slotted waveguide array with Hamming amplitude distribution is developed by it. The simulation results from HFSS (ANSYS®) verification of the antenna model are very near to the theoretical ones.

articleTitle: Bank branch electronic transformation
abstract: This paper presents the possibilities of using new types of banking transactions using the so-called BTAPI service, through migration from conventional to smart ATMs. BTAPI was developed as a service for the integration of multifunction ATMs with the Core Banking System for the needs of bank branch electronic transformation. Methodology that follows this transformation is based on the best features and benefits of a unified development process with the introduction of numerous principles of the agile software development. The proposed solution necessarily leads to additional unloading of the counters, automation of transactions, improvement of services to users, significant cost savings, attracting new ones as well as retention of existing clients.

articleTitle: Simple detection of network anomalies and topology control in ZigBee networks
abstract: The aim of this paper is to detect and mitigate two problems commonly observed in ZigBee networks. The first problem of oscillating link arises when device frequently changes parent devices used for routing packets, which consequently leads to additional time and resource waste. Second problem comes when a parent device has a dense cluster associated to it, in which case it becomes a bottleneck and can lead to traffic congestion and increased race for the radio resources. We provide 2 simple methods for topology control by modifying the transmission power of targeted devices. We demonstrate efficiency of proposed solution in detecting and mitigating issues on simple test topologies.

articleTitle: Analytical expressions for tuned feedback front end baseband optical receiver
abstract: The incorrect interpretation of the noise expressions of modified front end optical receivers is becoming more common and persistent. This paper presents improved analytical expressions for the calculation of: — 3dB cut-off bandwidth, transimpedance, noise equivalent bandwidths and equivalent input noise current densities of simple tuned optical baseband receiver front end built with BJTs and p-i-n diode. Coloured noise in the typical TIA receiver design caused by amplifier noise being referred through input transistor and RC network formed by photodiode and input amplifier. In the case of tuned front end, this arrangement is altered. Hence, classic noise expressions become invalid, which typically leads to overly optimistic noise numbers. Two mathematical models have been used to predict receiver sensitivity and to calculate the total noise for non-tuned and tuned front end optical receivers. The numerical results show receiver sensitivity improvement of 1dB to 2.2dB. However, the significance of the work presented here is in development and validation of referring noise in tuned front end baseband optical receiver as well as optimising the transfer function of the tuned feedback transimpedance.

articleTitle: Extending firmware support for new generation audio — Video receivers
abstract: This paper describes implementation of older audio coding algorithm on DSP processor used in audio-video receivers. Goal is to support missing audio format and improve the quality of reproduced sound.

articleTitle: A tool for displaying and analysis of video artifacts
abstract: Due to high capacity requirements, raw videos have to be compressed prior storage and transmission. However, compression and transmission processes introduce visible artifacts in video signal. Thus video quality needs to be monitored and evaluated continuously. In this work a new solution that enables the additional offline analysis of detected video artifacts is proposed. The solution is based on Real-time Audio and Video Artifacts Detection Tool (AVADT) and it displays the timeline accompanied by the markers of different artifacts in different moments of video stream. Furthermore, in the proposed solution the reproduction of video segments that contain detected artifacts is enabled. By using the proposed solution, video service providers can perform the extended analysis and check existing trends related to artifact occurrence during video streaming.

articleTitle: Multiscale gradient based digital radiography image registration
abstract: Two or more digital radiography images are stitched together after acquisition to represent the long bone anatomies. To perform the stitching, optimal translation between these composing images must be determined. We propose a method that combines anatomical and reference structure alignment. The proposed method is multiscale for faster computation, and gradient based to overcome intensity differences between images. Evaluation was performed on a dataset of medical and non-medical digital radiography image pairs. The average absolute difference of manually and automatically determined translation parameters is 1.29 pixels in the direction of the stitching and 2.29 pixels in the direction perpendicular to the direction of the stitching.

articleTitle: Uniform diffracted fields from non-conducting cylindrical surface by modified theory of physical optics
abstract: Modified Theory of Physical Optics (MTPO), is an innovative method by which the scattering (reflected and edge diffracted) fields can be calculated. Method is based on the current densities which are induced on scattering and aperture surfaces, stationary phase method and edge-point technique. Moreover, by MTPO edge diffraction can be found whereas physical optics has some deficiencies for this point. In this study, diffracted fields from a black cylinder have been calculated by MTPO. The obtained results have been numerically evaluated and verified with literature.

articleTitle: Improvements in the quality of service during vertical handovers between WiMAX and WLAN
abstract: This research is analyzing the heterogeneous networks (WLAN and WiMAX) and improving the decision algorithm during vertical handover between WLAN and WiMAX. The improvements include proposing new algorithm for vertical handover which will make the handover between the two networks seamless and will improve the qualities of the service for the users. The proposed algorithm is based on the WLAN overload, which is crucial while providing good quality of service to the mobile nodes. The other part in this paper is simulation of the scenario with the newly proposed algorithm and the existing MIH module in the 802.21 standard. The newly proposed algorithm avoids unnecessary vertical handovers from WiMAX to WLAN. At the end, the gathered results are analyzed and compared. During the simulation, measurements for the vertical handover latency, average throughput, jitter and packets received for each mobile node are done.

articleTitle: Implementation of a sub-system for DIAL verification within HbbTV test environment
abstract: The HbbTV 2.0 specification, published in 2015 by the Hybrid Broadcast Broadband TV (HbbTV) Association aims to integrate companion screen devices (mobile devices, tablets, etc) into HbbTV environment. This enables broadcasters to utilize second screen devices in order to show additional content-related information, stream broadcast content or launch and install native applications. In this paper we present an environment and tools used for verifying DIAL functionalities on HbbTV 2.0 compatible devices.

articleTitle: An analysis of passive relay station with back-to-back antenna for radio coverage improvement inside the buildings
abstract: The passive relay station implemented with two back-to-back antennas presents a possible, simple and cost-effective solution to achieve better radio-coverage quality inside the buildings. This paper presents theoretic analysis of the back-to-back solution for such application, followed by the experimental testing of one practical solution through the extensive measurement of achieved radio-coverage characteristics of an existing PMR network inside several electrical transformer station buildings. The measurement results confirmed, to a large extent, the results of the theoretical analysis, and it is concluded that the given solution, under the certain conditions, can be successfully applied for radio-coverage improvement inside the observed and similar type of buildings.

articleTitle: Spherical video player implementation using FFmpeg and SDL program support
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate an implementation model of the spherical video player. The first part refers to the transformation of the equirectangular projection create cubemap projection. Transformations are implemented using OpenCV library. The second part refers to the implementation of the video player. Processing video package is implemented using FFmpeg library. The user interface is implemented using SDL library.

articleTitle: Discrete approximations of continuous-time high-order system using Z- and delta transform
abstract: This paper investigates the model order reduction of the continuous-time high-order system using Skogestad “half rule” method and obtaining the discrete-time models in zand delta domain. The proposed approach is illustrating by the simulation example of a non-minimum phase highorder system. Some discretization effects at different sampling rates are analyzed.

articleTitle: Recognition of bimodal produced speech based on Support Vector Machines
abstract: This paper presents the results of experiments in recognition of whispered speech, as a specific mode of verbal communication, using SVM (Support Vector Machines) classifier. For training and testing purposes, part of the speech database Whi-Spe with male speakers has been exploited. In matched scenarios average word recognition rate was 99.3% (for normally phonated speech) and 97.8% (for whisper). In mismatched scenarios, recognition of whisper with training on normal speech utterances was 75.4%, whereas recognition of whisper-trained normal speech was with recognition rate of 81.3%.

articleTitle: The impact of radiation on volt-ampere characteristics of SiGe transistors
abstract: The article presents the comparison of the effects of the fast electrons with the energy of 6 MeV and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co gamma rays on the volt-ampere characteristics (VACs) of SiGe n-p-n transistors of SGB25V technology (the major ones for design of the analog ICs): the dependence of the static base current gain in the common-emitter (CE) configuration (β) on the emitter current (Ie), the output VAC in the CE configuration, the dependence of the voltage across the forward-biased base-emitter junction (Ube) on Ie.

articleTitle: Analiza neželjenih efekata u MIMO predajnicima sa više antenna
abstract: In this paper, an analysis of undesired effects in multi-antenna MIMO transmitters such as PA nonlinearity, IQ imbalance and nonlinear crosstalk is presented. An impact of these effects on signal quality is demonstrated through simulations. The obtained results are given in numerical and graphical forms using metrics in time and frequency domains.

articleTitle: An analysis of hierarchical multi-hop routing protocols for large wireless sensor networks
abstract: Wireless sensor networks represent technology for networking of sensor devices, as well as for other devices in IoT systems. The hierarchical routing protocols have many advantages when these networks are used in monitoring applications, with the energy efficient hierarchical multi-hop routing proposed for large scale networks that assures reliable data gathering in the non-ideal connectivity conditions. We here propose a modification of our previously designed multi-hop routing concept by employing clustering algorithm from HEED protocol in order to achieve uniformly placed clusters. The conducted analysis for several multi-hop protocols showed good performance of here proposed solution for ideal and non-ideal network connectivity.

articleTitle: Performance of the atto cell in LTE networks
abstract: The small cell provides cost effective solution to increase capacity of LTE networks and also covers deadzones of macro cells. Downlink signal of small cell suffers from that of macro cell because it uses same frequency of macro cell. Recently, the Atto cell as a small cell solution for home mobile networks is introduced by mobile operators. This article provides the performance evaluation of the Atto cell such as SINR (Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio) and throughput. Also, we propose optimal installation position between the Atto cell and macro cell.

articleTitle: Greedy forwarding for hyperbolic space in MANET
abstract: A new routing method based on greedy advancement and hyperbolic transformation is proposed. In order to avoid the local minimum problem, bit addressing is proposed using a tree-like connection graph. Unlike the existing hyperbolic address spaces, the new distance metric is equal to the hops number of transitions over the graph. An algorithm for assigning variable-length bit addresses to a given node configuration has been developed. The process of assigning hyperbolic addresses is illustrated. A comparative performance analysis for a new routing method and traditional approaches is then performed.

articleTitle: Kanban-based framework for analysis of heterogeneous academic data
abstract: Bibliometric techniques are widely used to study the factors leading to successful research, though this is not without its challenges. One notable problem is that academic data is very diverse, and involves complex interactions between many different entities and players. In this paper, a novel framework for analyzing heterogeneous academic data is proposed. While such a framework would have many different applications, this paper focuses on the design of an academic recommendation system, which is one interesting use case for this framework.

articleTitle: Initiating and tracking social actions to adapt and improve smart city's business processes
abstract: This paper presents Business-2-Social (B2S) platform. It is a Web-based application that provides connection of a smart city's components, namely business processes, Internet of Things (IoT), and social networks. B2S collects and processes IoT-related data in preparation of supporting the decision makers. Based on IoT data and defined guidelines, B2S automatically initiates social actions and collects citizens' feedback. The objective is to drive the interactions between smart cities and citizens so that necessary services are offered.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis of electromagnetic radiation originating from 802.11a/g WLAN devices
abstract: The experimental analysis of the electromagnetic radiation originating from WLAN devices was carried out on the laboratory topology of the WLAN, by measuring the electric field strength originating from the access point on the one hand and the WLAN client on the other. The results of the measurement show that electromagnetic radiation largely depends on the type of used service, and that the obtained values are significantly below the prescribed reference limits.

articleTitle: Improving FDTD algorithm performance using block floating-point
abstract: FDTD (finite-difference time-domain) algorithm is a memory intensive problem which requires more memory access in comparison to computing intensive problems. Existing FDTD solutions use either floating-point or fixed-point arithmetic. Floating-point solutions are less memory intensive but require more computation. Fixed-point solutions are the opposite - simpler computation but use up more memory bandwidth for the same precision. The method chosen in this paper includes using block floating-point arithmetic which is the middle ground. This approach requires less computation than floating-point arithmetic while at the same time using less memory access than plain fixed-point. The FDTD algorithm is converted from floating to fixed-point and then to block floating-point. The precision and memory access performance is compared.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic nature of “anomalous” runaway electrons in fast gas discharges
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive theoretical explanation of the physical phenomenon of runaway electrons having “anomalous” energies in nanosecond gas discharges. By using the example of a simple model problem of a single electron motion in the traveling wave electric field, it was shown that electron is capable to gain an energy much greater than the maximum of applied voltage multiplied by the electron charge. The detailed kinetic calculation in terms of numerical solution of Maxwell-Boltzmann system of equations is given further for the important case of one-dimensional axisymmetric gas diode. The obtained results are in good agreement with the existing experimental data.

articleTitle: Mobile device real time software solution for automated testing with robotic arm
abstract: Software solution for testing of mobile devices using automated robotic arm is presented in this paper. Algorithm is developed and implemented for precise positioning of robotic arm in the workspace, it performs touch operation on predefined touch screen grid. Software is capable of handling different screen sizes and overall mobile device dimensions. Final solution testing is performed on commercially available mobile device.

articleTitle: Development of the MIPS32 optimizing compiler for ART
abstract: Applications for Android operating system are usually developed in Java programming language. Although traditional Java virtual machines use just-in-time compilation, Android uses ahead-of-time compilation. Two ahead-of-time compilers were developed for Android so far, the quick compiler and the optimizing compiler. This paper describes implementation of the optimizing compiler for MIPS32 architecture.

articleTitle: High-pass filter consisting of two L-type resonators and two interdigitated capacitors
abstract: The article deals with the study and description of a high-pass filter. This filter structure is based on two similar L-type resonators and a microstrip transmission line located on the substrate side opposite to resonators with two identical series connected interdigitated capacitors. The filter is installed on the substrate made of FR-4, with dielectric constant ε=4.4 and thickness h=1.5 mm. The filter structural design and numerical computation were performed with the use of a specialized Ansoft HFSS program. The area of the filter designed with the use of an EM simulations program equals 40 × 50 = 2000 mm2. Results of the numerical simulation allowed producing a prototype with the use of circuit boards etching technique. Vector network analyzer helped to achieve an amplitude response curve that only slightly differs from the simulation results.

articleTitle: Improved belief propagation based on the estimation backtracking
abstract: We propose a general method to improve the decoding performance of hard-decision and soft-decision belief propagation decoders. The performance of the proposed algorithm is tested on MacKay's widely known LDPC (504,252) code, CCSDS LDPC (256,128) and our irregular LDPC (128,64) code. The bit error rate indicated by our novel solution is up to five times lower for a particular signal-to-noise ratio of tested codes measured through AWGN simulations. Furthermore, a decoding time required for the same bit error rate as the bit error rate of a traditional BP decoder is up to three times lower when our approach is used in a non-pipelined implementation.

articleTitle: Stable switching control of DC-DC converters
abstract: This paper presents an approach to construct nonlinear control for switching DC-DC converters. What is presented are commonly used control methods and they are compared with nonlinear methods: sliding-mode control, hysteresis control and control using polytopic Lyapunov functions. In addition, an experimental realization of the sliding-mode controlled Buck converter is described in detail.

articleTitle: Adapting UBIFS file system to android operating system requirements
abstract: This paper describes the process and modifications necessary for UBIFS file system to properly function under Android Nougat. These modifications refer to BLKROSET ioctl() (input/output control) support and the required modes for fallocate() system call. All modifications have been performed on Android flavored Linux kernel, version 3.18. Validation has been performed by executing CTS test suite, executing LTP test suite and comparing custom test results to those of EXT4 file system.

articleTitle: UWB positioning system for elderly persons tracking in IONIS AAL platform
abstract: UWB (Ultra Wideband) indoor positioning system infrastructure is typically composed of anchor nodes deployed in the area covered by the system. The nodes are usually mounted as high as possible to provide better propagation conditions. The paper proposes a solution consisting in deploying anchors directly at the floor level. The paper includes a description of investigation of such system. The results of positioning are presented and discussed. The first path signal component propagation was experimentally investigated. Results of measurements are used for positioning system's performance analysis.

articleTitle: Dual cavity Ku-band antenna for SatCom applications
abstract: Circular waveguide to dual-cavity transition is proposed for wideband, high gain, high aperture efficiency and low profile (60.6 mm) antenna. Target bandwidth is Ku band downlink and uplink frequency bands. Simulation result shows 40% (10-15 GHz) fractional bandwidth at VSWR<;1.5. Propose antenna has minimum 11.3 dBi gain at downlink band and minimum 12.4 dBi at uplink band. Aperture efficiency is better than 65% throughout the band. The structure offers a good alternative to standard gain horn antennas but with much less antenna profile. It can be used in phased array applications as well.

articleTitle: One solution for extension of the system for recording multimedial content on Android based devices
abstract: In the last ten years mass transition from analog to digital television led to great advancements in the development of set-top box devices and smart TVs. Parallel to this advancement the influence of Android grew and it very quickly became one of the most commonly used systems on these devices. Since the appearance of first set-top box devices their core functionalities were reproduction and recording of TV content. Android supports reproduction and recording of MPEG-4, WebM and 3GP formats and only reproduction of MPEG-TS format, which is the most abundant format in the area of digital television — it is used for terrestrial, cable and satellite transmission. The goal of this paper is the extension of the system for recording multimedial content inside of Android, so that recording of MPEG-TS would be supported as well.

articleTitle: nutIE — A modern open source natural language processing toolkit
abstract: Nowadays, there are many tools and applications available that use novel machine learning algorithms, but only few tools exist that bridge the gap between the computer scientists and general public. The latter especially holds for the field of natural language processing. Therefore in this paper we present a new information extraction toolkit, called nutIE, that offers a frontend for end-to-end text analysis using a modern javascript-based web application. The core of the toolkit includes all the high-level information extraction techniques with supporting preprocessing and evaluation methods. All these can be accessed by a Scala programmatic API or an arbitrary third-party application via REST interface. It has already been shown that the integrated toolkit's algorithms achieve state-of-the art results. The toolkit is currently applied at international text processing projects and courses.

articleTitle: Investigation on temporal skewing among O-CDMA code carriers under fiber temperature variations
abstract: Experimental investigation has been conducted on the influence of optical fiber temperature variations on Two Dimension Wavelength/Hopping Time/Spreading Incoherent Optical Code Division Multiple Access (2D-WH/TS iOCDMA) codes. Our experimental results show that in the literature reported approaches assuming a temperature induced coefficient Dtemp in optical fiber being a constant are only accurate when the selection of code carriers' wavelengths is from a relatively narrow spectral interval. This paper shows that if the selection of code carriers' wavelengths is from a wider spectral interval, neglecting to mitigate the wavelength dependency of D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">temp</sub> would have a significant impact on the recovered iOCDMA Autocorrelation function.

articleTitle: Solar storm detecting by integrated magnetometer based on anisotropic magnetoresistivity
abstract: This paper deals with the geomagnetic field measurement by integrated sensor based on principle of anisotropic magnetoresistivity (AMR). The geomagnetic field measurements require very precise instrumentation which is mostly spacious. On the other hand, the chosen magnetometer - HMC5883L - is very tiny but suffers from lower resolution and high noise floor. The objective is to examine possibility of geomagnetism investigation made by an integrated widespread magnetometer, to evaluate its precision and to detect some outer space events by geomagnetism observations. There was proposed and constructed measuring device including AMR chip. The measuring device including the AMR chip was proposed and produced. A long-term measurement was recorded in collaboration with the geomagnetic observatory Budkov, Czech Republic (Institute of Geophysics of the CAS, v. v. i.; INTERMAGNET). The post-processing was designed in order to suppress sensor noise and temp-drift. The post-processing used was standardized by INTERMAGNET especially for geomagnetic observatories. Finally, with the constructed device there were detected the day-night variations of the Earth magnetic field and a solar storm of 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> grade of k-index.

articleTitle: A novel antenna for GPS and Iridium satellite phone applications in M2M communication
abstract: The Archimedean spiral antenna is a popular type of selfcomplementary antenna. This study presents a two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna for GPS and Iridium applications. Circular symmetrical artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is used as a ground plane in low-profile two-arm spiral antenna design. Proposed AMC structure enhanced the gain and axial ratio characteristics of traditional sipral antenna. Simulation results show good axial ratio, impedance match and stable gain for both operation bands.

articleTitle: One solution for safe playback of multimedia content on Android-based systems
abstract: Android is an open-source software that became popular on mobile devices, but lately, can be found on other platforms like television and set-top box devices. With the development of internet television and a possibility for two-way communication between client and content provider, there is a lot of room for the development of modern methods for protection of audio and video streams. A couple of notable implementations for data protection systems are present on the market today. Unfortunately, the source code of these implementations is not available online, which makes it difficult to develop new systems for data protection. This paper presents one solution for safe playback of multimedia content on Android-based systems realized using the trusted execution environment.

articleTitle: Network parameters applicable in detection of infrastructure level DDoS attacks
abstract: Distributed denial of service attacks represent continuous threat to availability of information and communication resources. This research conducted the analysis of relevant scientific literature and synthesize parameters on packet and traffic flow level applicable for detection of infrastructure layer DDoS attacks. It is concluded that packet level detection uses two or more parameters while traffic flow level detection often used only one parameter which makes it more convenient and resource efficient approach in DDoS detection.

articleTitle: Dual harmonic anti-scatter grid artefact removal for digital radiography
abstract: Use of low density anti-scatter grids with modern high resolution digital radiography detectors produces artefacts in the form of periodic stripes. We propose an approach for anti-scatter grid artefact removal in diagnostic digital radiography images. The approach is based on dual homomorphic filtering of spectral harmonics. We show that existing single harmonic methods are unable to remove periodic image artefacts completely, leaving image quality compromised. Adopting the conventional multiplicative grid model of image formation, we show that simple extension of the one harmonic approach leads to further artefacts and propose an alternative second harmonic removal filter. It is shown that the proposed algorithm produces superior image quality, both for non-clinical and clinical diagnostic x-ray images, compared to only first harmonic removal used in state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Poincare diagram based analysis of vital signals
abstract: Analysis of the vital signals is of great importance for monitoring a patient's condition. The most frequently analyzed vital signal is electrocardiogram. There are many methods in literature that give different insights into heart variability. This paper provides parameters calculated on signals from two referent Physionet databases. The first one contains signals without pathological indications, while the other contains those with pathological indications. All parameters are calculated in time domain. Nonlinear methods provide better insight into analyzed signals. Hence, the Poincare diagram is constructed over all electrocardiograms from the database.

articleTitle: Resistive switching effects in nanomaterials based memristors
abstract: Presented research results aim to provide contribution in deeper understanding of physical mechanisms which drives resistive switching effect in memristors, the fourth fundamental element introduced in electronic circuit theory. Here, we report testing results for three classes of memristors: valence change memories, ferroelectric and mulitferroic memristors. The objective of the testing was to reveal electrical and structural properties and to identify different transport effects within the devices. Analyzed components can be used in novel computing paradigms such as neuromorphic and bioinspired computation, bioelectronics and non-volatile memories.

articleTitle: Proposal of approach to organizational project management in the process of digital transformation
abstract: The paper presents a proposal for approach to organizational project management in permanent organizations, in the context of the upcoming digital transformation. Considering the fact that the issue of digital transformation is primarily a matter of the organization's strategy, and as the primary goal of organizational project management is the realization of it, an proposed approach represents enhancement primarily in the context of using newer achievements in project management, and consequently also changes in other areas. In addition, the role of the Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO) has been modified and described briefly.

articleTitle: Expert system for infrared heating panel optimization
abstract: This paper is focused on the development of an expert system able to add flexibility to the residential building heating system The proposed solution is adjusted to the Infrared Heating Panel's technology but it can be adapted also for other heating devices. The experimental results prove that our method can improve life quality and also reduce consumption.

articleTitle: Predlog dizajna antene za WiFi podvodne komunikacije
abstract: Monitoring kvaliteta vodene životne sredine uslovljava porast bežičnih podvodnih senzorskih mreža sa naglaskom na komunikaciju putem elektromagnetnih talasa. Proučavanjem karakteristika morske vode i njenog uticaja na slabljenje elektromagnetnih talasa, dovodi do zaključka da je dizajn odgovarajuće antene ključan za funkcionisanje podvodnog komunikacionog sistema. Rad na nižim frekvencijama omogućava komunikaciju na većim rastojanjima, ali zahtijeva antenu velike dimenzije, dok komunikacija na visokim frekvencijama omogućava veliku brzinu prenosa ali je ograničena na malo rastojanje. S obzirom na zahtijeve za brzinom prenosa podataka i veličinom antene, predlažemo upotrebu opsega na 2.4 GHz. U ovom radu izvršena je analiza parametara morske vode uzete sa više lokacija u Bokokotorskom zalivu i analiziran je njen uticaj na prostiranje elektromagnetnih talasa i predložen simulacioni model antene za podvodnu komunikaciju u uslovima promjenljive provodnosti.

articleTitle: Zero-forcing beamforming user grouping algorithms in massive MIMO systems
abstract: In this paper an analysis of different User Grouping algorithms with Zero-Forcing Beamforming technique for IoT oriented massive MIMO systems is presented. The capacity-based algorithms with both non-overlapping and overlapping user grouping are observed. The algorithm working principles are outlined and the complexity of each of the algorithm is evaluated. Additionally, a comparative performance analysis is performed. The results show that a better performance of the massive MIMO system is achieved with the algorithms based on overlapping user grouping approach compared to the algorithms based on non-overlapping user grouping approach.

articleTitle: DAPS — A web based system for predicting IoT sensor data
abstract: IoT systems are expected to generate voluminous raw sensor measurements that require high bandwidths to be transmitted to the clouds. IoT data prediction is one solution to this issue. Yet, many algorithms based on different models for times series prediction can be used for this purpose. IoT developers have to choose among many of them, since they perform differently for different sensor measurements. In this paper, we present DAta Prediction System (DAPS), a web-based online tool that helps IoT developers to choose the most suitable data prediction algorithms for their application.

articleTitle: Extending implementation of dial protocol on Android based devices
abstract: Today, there is a need to emit any kind and any format of multimedia on any interactive device. Zero configuration protocols, where no special device pairing is nedeed, find their role in such market. This work represents solution which implements such protocol, which full name is Discovery and Launch (DIAL) protocol.

articleTitle: Formation of optimal Boolean functions for analog-digital conversion
abstract: This paper describes a situation in which the function obtained from an analog-to-digital conversion is considered a partially-certain function. In this case it is possible to neglect the least significant bits and therefore redefine them arbitrarily. A realization of proposed method simplifies the further processing of the received signal, and saves hardware consumption at designing and usage of hardware and software systems that include analog-to-digital converters.

articleTitle: Improving cellular coverage by using UAVS
abstract: Cellular covering of big events can be sometimes difficult, due to the fact that places of happening in network planning are not assumed to be so crowded. Also, in present social networks one of the key characteristics is tremendous increasing of uplink live streams. In these situations it is often critical to provide appropriate quality of service. A solution for meeting these requirements is implementation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that can act as relays between base station (BS) and mobile units (MUs). Here, we considered several practical scenarios for UAVs implementation, for distributed realization of space diversity, i.e. multiple input multiple output (MIMO) channel between MUs and BS.

articleTitle: Analysis of the possibility of implementing a high density backhaul system in the E-band
abstract: Number of mobile users, therefore need of mobile operators to increase capacity of backhaul system, is constantly increasing. E-band is particularly interesting for backhaul due to favorable propagation characteristics, bandwidth, use of highly directional small diameter antennas with high gain, which ensures transmission of large amounts of data. In this paper characteristics of E-band were considered, simulation of real network was performed and conclusions on possibility of using this band for 4G/5G backhaul were made.

articleTitle: Optimization of NLLS algorithm using matrix Algebra: Application on SAR tomography
abstract: The general problem of multiple signal sources detection using an array of sensors, with the particular case of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Tomography is approached in this paper. A detection algorithm which generates accurate results but it's computationally demanding, sup-GLRT (Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test with support estimation), is discussed. Main objective consists in applying matrix algebra for optimization of 2D Non-Linear Least Squares (NLLS) search implementation, the most demanding part of the detector. Results of the detection algorithm on a dataset of high resolution SAR images are presented. Performance of the proposed optimization method is assessed by comparison of algorithm implementation times.

articleTitle: Influence of transmission power on wireless mesh network quality
abstract: Studies in this paper describe how transmission power influences communication quality in wireless mesh networks. Firstly by describing theoretical basis, gathering neccecery information and performing measurements which were latter analyzed. At the very end of this paper we proposed a new solution to this problem and the means of how it would benefit the whole wireless communication process.
